summary: Refuse looping MP4 edits explicitly instead of silently treating them as finite
before: After correcting a test-harness enum match (compile log retained separately), the runtime baseline has 1 passing finite trim test and 2 failing tests. Both parser wrappers accept six loop/reserved flag witnesses and native playback accepts a loop as a finite trim.
after: 49 distinct checks pass in 11 integration targets, including 3 new tests. Zero-flag V0/V1 trim controls retain exact analytic YUV, software RGB, PTS/duration, random seeks, rewind and EOF. Related finite/open-ended video/audio edits, variable rates, decode-only coverage, header sizes and seek I/O remain green. Locked offline no-default-features core build check passes.
tests_run: cargo test --locked --offline --no-default-features --features player --no-fail-fast --test mp4_edit_loop --test mp4_edit_window_eof --test mp4_decode_only_seek --test mp4_empty_tail --test mp4_open_ended_edit --test mp4_open_ended_edit_audio --test mp4_fixed_audio_edits --test mp4_variable_rate_edits --test mp4_time_header_sizes --test mp4_tfdt_flags --test mp4_seek_io_regressions
limitations: No full project-wide green claim; historical unrelated failures remain separate.
Dedicated acceptance uses software decoding; related existing worker tests do not qualify physical GPU parity.
uncounted: Related finite edit acceptance and resource controls
